description: A senior vice president and general counsel must approve the company's written response to a medical-device regulator's deficiency letter and set the product, quality, commercial, and data-submission terms of that response, with input from regulatory, quality, commercial, and privacy specialists.

agents.name: Elena Morris
agents.role: Senior Vice President and General Counsel

shared_context.S1: The company received a deficiency letter concerning its marketed pediatric monitoring device, and the written response is due to the regulator in 30 calendar days.
shared_context.S2: The regulator asks the company to clarify the device's software scope, manufacturing controls, pediatric labeling, and handling of supporting patient data.
shared_context.S3: A draft response has been circulated internally, but it has not yet been approved or submitted.
shared_context.S4: The circulated draft leaves unresolved questions about software scope, lot disposition, the pediatric indication, and the patient-data fields to be included.

PF1.text: Nikhil received a written follow-up from the regulator after a technical call, confirming that the response must be limited to software version 4.2 and must include an answer matrix with exactly six question rows; he saved the message in the regulatory mailbox but has not incorporated it into the circulated draft.

PF2.text: Dana's review of the latest quality-audit packet found calibration deviations in lots L17 and L18; those two lots must be placed on hold and investigated before any release, but the finding has not been added to the response's corrective-action section.

PF3.text: Marisol confirmed in the hospital customer's contract file that the customer may terminate if the company's regulatory response withdraws or narrows the pediatric indication; the response must preserve the pediatric indication rather than propose withdrawing it.

PF4.text: Theo's privacy review of the regulator's requested data confirmed that the submission may contain only deidentified aggregate data, with suppression of every reporting cell representing fewer than 10 patients; the draft currently does not specify either restriction.

acceptance_conditions: The response must be limited to software version 4.2.
The response must contain exactly six question rows in its answer matrix.
Lots L17 and L18 must be placed on hold and investigated before release.
The response must preserve the pediatric indication.
The submitted data must be deidentified aggregate data only.
Every reporting cell representing fewer than 10 patients must be suppressed.
The filing must include a quality hold and investigation commitment targeting lots L17 and L18.
The filing must include a quality hold and investigation commitment.

content_checks.C5: decisions['data_submission_mode'] in ['deidentified_aggregate', 'deidentified aggregate data only', 'Deidentified aggregate data only']
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'quality_hold_and_investigation' and c['target'] == 'L17 and L18' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'quality_hold_and_investigation' for c in commitments) or any(c['type'] == 'corrective_action' for c in commitments) or any(c['type'] == 'lot_disposition' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The regulator's follow-up changes the response scope to software version 4.2 only and changes the answer matrix to exactly six rows.
The quality-audit finding changes the disposition of lots L17 and L18 to a required hold, investigation, and corrective-action commitment specifically targeting both lots.
The customer's termination right changes the labeling choice to preserving the pediatric indication rather than withdrawing or narrowing it.
The privacy review changes the data terms to deidentified aggregate data only and requires suppression of every cell with fewer than 10 patients.
